title: Microsoft Edge: top sites in the Edge search bar
summary: The roadmap facts, policy paths and registry references check out. However, the briefing states that the visibility policy applies to Microsoft account profiles without acknowledging that the same Microsoft reference explicitly marks those profiles unsupported; administrators should not rely on that applicability claim until the documentation conflict is resolved.

claims.claim: No dedicated Microsoft Learn feature page for search bar Top Sites was found.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Top Sites" "search bar" Microsoft Edge'; opened both quick links policy references and searched the Edge policy index. Results describe the policies, mobile ManagedTopSites, other surfaces and unrelated release notes, not a dedicated desktop feature page.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state of search bar Top Sites is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge search bar Top Sites default enabled license price rollout version hide sites policy'; read both quick links references and SearchbarAllowed. The NTP quick links default and search bar availability do not state the arrival default of this new list.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence or entitlement requirement for this feature was found.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Microsoft Edge for Business" licensing requirements top sites' and '"Edge" "search bar" "top sites" license pricing'; read Edge for Business and both quick links references. Results name licences for sync and security services, not this feature or basic browser use.

claims.claim: No consumption meter for this feature is published in the material found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge search bar Top Sites default enabled license price rollout version hide sites policy' and '"Edge" "search bar" "top sites" license pricing'; read both quick links policies and Edge for Business. No feature meter was found.

claims.claim: No price for this feature is published in the material found.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Edge" "search bar" "top sites" license pricing'; read both quick links policies and Edge for Business. Neither the record nor those pages names a feature price; search results concerned unrelated pricing and software terms.

claims.claim: The cited sources describe no spending cap for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge search bar Top Sites spending cap budget control storage cost'; read both quick links policies, Edge for Business, the record and relevant Edge policy-index entries. None describes a feature spending cap.

claims.claim: The cited sources describe no budget control for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge search bar Top Sites spending cap budget control storage cost'; read both quick links references, Edge for Business and the record, and searched relevant policy-index entries. These sources describe no feature budget control.

claims.claim: The cited sources describe no storage cost for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge search bar Top Sites spending cap budget control storage cost'; read both quick links references, Edge for Business and the roadmap record. None describes a feature storage cost.

claims.claim: The material found does not state whether search bar Top Sites derives its own list from browsing history.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge "top sites" "search bar" "browsing history"'; read NewTabPageManagedQuickLinks. It describes the history-based NTP list and managed tiles included in search bar Top Sites, not the source of the latter's other entries.

claims.claim: The sources do not identify the Edge version or first release channel for search bar Top Sites.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Edge" "Top Sites" "search bar" default version rollout history hide policy'; read both quick links references and returned release-note excerpts. The policy support versions do not identify the introduction version of search bar Top Sites.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe rollout staging for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Edge" "Top Sites" "search bar" default version rollout history hide policy'; read both quick links references, the record and returned release-note excerpts. No staging by tenant, profile or channel for this feature was found.

claims.claim: Neither quick links reference describes a setting that governs only the search bar Top Sites list.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge "top sites" "search bar" "hide" policy users'; read both quick links references and SearchbarAllowed, and searched the policy index. Quick links controls also affect NTP; SearchbarAllowed controls the entire search bar, not only its Top Sites list.

claims.claim: The pages do not document a control preventing users from hiding individual search bar sites.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Edge "top sites" "search bar" "hide" policy users'; read both quick links references and SearchbarAllowed. Mandatory managed tiles cannot be deleted, but no text states that users cannot hide individual search bar sites.

claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies no new data-access, sign-in or permission requirement.
claims.quote: Adding easy access to top sites in Edge search bar on desktop. Users can add, edit, remove, or hide top sites. Admins can control available to this feature using the NewTabPageManagedQuickLinks and NewTabPageQuickLinksEnabled policies.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes user-controlled list actions, not autonomous action on a user's behalf.
claims.quote: Users can add, edit, remove, or hide top sites.
